title: Dogs: Bullets & Carnage
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a dystopian European city scarred by crime and genetic experimentation, four antihero gunmen and swordfighters, among them Heine, Badou and Naoto, cross paths while searching for a way into 'the Below' to uncover their pasts. Their stories involve the mafia, 'Lost Children' created by experiments, and a killer with a black sword.
life_message: Wounded outsiders keep fighting to learn the truth about who made them what they are.

Fashion-forward character designs noted by reviewers; no tie-ins.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Gunmen and swordfighters settle scores personally, outside any law.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Loners operating in a lawless underground city.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Small loyalties and personal pasts matter more than society.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Mafia hierarchies exist but heroes are independent.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Biopunk science and experiments shape the world.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival in a brutal city; style is expressive but life is precarious.

folkways.japan: Draws on Western crime-film and gun-action aesthetics more than Japanese social norms.

delivery.evidence: ANN calls it style over substance with tough-guy clichés (via Wikipedia); no stated message.
delivery.note: Reviewers focus on visual style; whatever message it has must be inferred.

winners_losers: The four antiheroes get the sympathy; the mafia and experimenters are the antagonists.
